test_title: RRB Technician Grade III Official Paper (Held On: 30 Dec, 2024 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: The cost incurred by Manjit to produce an item in the factory was ₹2,000. He had to spend 10% of the production cost incurred on the item in the factory to transport it to the showroom. He sold the item from the showroom at a price that was 15% above the total cost incurred by Manjit in the production and transportation of the item. What was the price at which Manjit sold the item from the showroom?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

**Total Cost** = Production Cost × 1.10 (as transport is 10%)

**Selling Price** = Total Cost × 1.15 (as profit is 15%)

**Selling Price** = 2000 × 1.10 × 1.15 = 2000 × 1.265

**Selling Price** = 2530

**∴ The correct answer is ₹2,530.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Production Cost = ₹2,000 | Transport = 10% of Production | Profit = 15% on Total Cost

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/339362eaaff094c62a67d3b06f942a879e25688ea9c004f3137330248f8d00c8.png] 

⇒ **Transportation Cost** = 10% of ₹2,000 = (10/100) × 2000 = ₹200

⇒ **Total Cost Incurred** = Production Cost + Transportation Cost = ₹2,000 + ₹200 = ₹2,200

⇒ **Markup/Profit** = 15% of Total Cost = (15/100) × 2200 = ₹330

⇒ **Selling Price** = Total Cost + Profit = ₹2,200 + ₹330 = ₹2,530

**∴ The correct answer is ₹2,530.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Total Cost Concept

Total cost includes the factory production cost plus all **overhead expenses** like transportation, taxes, and labor incurred before the sale.

Successive Percentage Increase

If a value is increased by x% and then by y%, the final value is Base × (1 + x/100) × (1 + y/100).

Markup Percentage

Markup % = (Selling Price − Cost Price) ÷ Cost Price × 100. In this case, the profit acts as the markup on the final cost.
